answer: A tundra observatory imaging a nebula through a trellis of antenna supports could weight agents by measured storage capacity. Before rewards, each agent commits to a uniquely encoded replica keyed to its identity; unpredictable spot challenges require timely proofs of stored chunks. Encoding prevents one copy from answering for many aliases, while deadlines limit fetching on demand. Additional identities therefore require additional disk space, encoding work and power, making influence scale with resources rather than names.
